To sync rules, keep GodViewer running in the background before you edit views in a target app.
Get GodViewer working in a few steps
Root your device and install a working LSPosed (or compatible Xposed) framework. Reboot after installation.
Open LSPosed → Modules → enable GodViewer. You only need to scope the target apps you want to edit — the host app itself does not need to be in scope.
Add the apps you want to inspect to the module scope, then force-stop those apps (or reboot) so hooks load cleanly.

Open a scoped app, enable edit mode from the GodViewer notification or entry, tap a view, adjust size / margin / padding / visibility / text / image, then Apply. Rules are saved inside the target app and replay after restart.

• Synced rules on the Rules tab are read-only mirrors pushed when a target saves rules.
• Keep this app process alive (e.g. in recents) if you want mirrors to arrive reliably.
• Only the target apps you edit need notification permission (for the edit-mode control). GodViewer itself does not request notification permission.
• Corrupt rule files are ignored safely and will not crash the target app.
Remove the launcher shortcut. Reopen via the persistent notification, LSPosed module settings, or the system app list.

Hide the desktop icon?

Afterwards you can reopen GodViewer from:
• The persistent notification
• LSPosed → Modules → GodViewer → settings/gear
• System settings → Apps
Desktop icon hidden. Use the notification or LSPosed module settings to reopen.
